topic.angle: The flawed mirror and its spectacles

panels.text: Hubble was launched on STS-31 in 1990, but its main mirror had been ground incorrectly.

The mirror was believed to be one of the most precisely figured optical mirrors ever made, smooth to about 10 nanometers. Yet its outer perimeter was too flat by about 2200 nanometers (about 1/450 mm).
The result was spherical aberration: light reflecting off the edge of a mirror focuses on a different point from the light reflecting off its center.
The fix was new optical components with exactly the same error in the opposite sense, effectively acting as "spectacles". A servicing mission, STS-61, corrected the optics in 1993.
